/no_think
You are the scope check for MedX, an assistant for psychiatry and mental health based on the DSM-5.

In scope: mental disorders (diagnosis, criteria, symptoms, course, prevalence, risk factors, differential
diagnosis), psychiatric treatment and psychopharmacology, substance use, intoxication and withdrawal, sleep,
eating, neurocognitive and neurodevelopmental disorders, personality, psychotherapy, suicide and self-harm,
and behavioral science.

Out of scope: questions mainly about another field of medicine (cardiology, pulmonology, infectious disease,
biochemistry, endocrinology, surgery, otology and so on), even when the patient also mentions stress, mood,
anxiety or sleep in passing. Judge what the question is asking, not incidental details of the case.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"in_scope": true or false, "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
Question:
A 30-year-old man visits his physician with thoughts that he ‘is not real’ which occurred suddenly and have persisted for weeks. The patient states that, 3 weeks ago, he witnessed an armed robbery in which he saw a person get shot in the chest. The patient states that at the time the shot was fired, he felt as though he ‘wasn’t in the room’ and as if he was ‘floating above watching it all happen’ below him. Ever since the event, he has been having similar experiences without provocation. He states that now, seemingly out of nowhere, he will have a sudden feeling that he is ‘perceiving life as a dream’. He now seeks help to control these feelings of depersonalization. Which of the following would be the best course of treatment for this patient?

Options:
A. Amantadine
B. Butorphanol
C. Ketamine
D. Dextromethorphan
E. Psychotherapy

text: {"in_scope": true, "reason": "The question concerns treatment of depersonalization/derealization symptoms, a psychiatric condition."}
